notes:
- A reopened thread picks up at the newest end: Dismissing a comment sheet and opening it again refreshed the oldest page you had scrolled back to and replaced the whole window with it, so the conversation appeared to jump backwards and the newest comments vanished. The rows already in hand stay on screen and the newest page is refreshed instead; if comments kept arriving while the sheet was closed, the pages after it are fetched as well, so the thread never reopens with a conversation missing from the middle. Message threads reopen the same way, because they are drawn by the same sheet.
- Tapping an image opens the picture: An image with no link around it did nothing when tapped, while the same comment on AniList opens the picture itself. Every embedded image now presses and opens - its link when the author wrapped one around it, and the image address otherwise - in bios, comments, messages and spoilers alike.
- The install permission opens the right Settings screen: The updater's button for allowing installs built its Settings intent without the flag that starting an activity from an application context needs. The launch threw, the throw was swallowed, and the dialog reported "This device has no Settings app" on phones whose Settings app was fine. The screen opens now, and a device whose Settings app does not offer the per-app install screen falls back to AniSequel's own app details page, where the same switch lives.
- GIF search finds a series by its name: Searching a show - Spice and Wolf, Kaguya-sama - answered nothing, because a booru matches tags rather than sentences: the words you typed are ANDed together and no post carries both, while the series lives under one tag you could not be expected to know. The picker now asks a search three ways before it calls it a miss: your words as tags, the whole phrase as one tag, and then your first word as a prefix, which is what reaches the series when neither of the first two exists as a tag. The empty search offers two rows instead of a blinking cursor - reactions for the feeling you want, series for the show you have in mind, every one checked against the live index - and the field says which index you are searching.
- An Older page leaves you where you were: Loading older comments put a page of them above the row you were reading, and the list kept its index - so the conversation slid downwards under your eyes and the comment you had been reading left the screen. The thread now holds your place, to the pixel. Two related jumps are gone as well: quoting a comment and cancelling went back to the newest message instead of the five pages you had walked up to, and the scroll after you posted landed on somebody else's comment when the thread had scrolled up first.
- A Refresh button in the comment header: An open thread asked AniList for new comments every fifteen seconds, and there was no way to ask now. The header has a Refresh control, and beside it the last time the thread was checked, so the thread tells you how old what you are reading is. Two taps in a row are one request, because AniList holds each account at about thirty requests a minute and every other screen in the app spends from the same purse.
- Photos get the size and framing commands: A picked GIF could be inserted at 220, at 50%, centred or behind a spoiler; a picked photo went in at the site's full width with no control at all, even though the markup for both is the same. The size and framing row now sits above the attach button too, so a screenshot can go in small and hidden exactly like a reaction can, and the choice is kept for each draft you are writing.
- Attached photos show up on AniList now: A photo that uploaded through one of the fallback hosts stored fine and then refused to display: that host answers a request carrying AniList's own address with a dropped connection, so the picture looked right in this app and was a broken image for everybody reading the comment on the site. The hosts are now tried in the order that keeps the file readable where it is used, and if a photo does land on a host the site cannot read, the composer says so on the spot instead of letting you find out from somebody else's reply.
- A bio keeps the images it was written around: A profile bio is mostly pictures - a banner strip, a GIF between two headings, a spoilered reveal - and three things went wrong reading one. An image written inside formatting, like a GIF in a bold heading line, was not recognised as an image at all, so it printed its alt text as a link while the same bio on AniList animated. The size the author gave an image was thrown away: the API returns a sized image as HTML with a width attribute, the parser read only the address and the caption, and a bio built from a full-width banner and two small strips came out as three full-column slabs. And a bio whose only image sat inside a centred span, a spoiler or a quoted comment was treated as having no image at all, so it was collapsed behind "Show more" and the picture landed below the clip. Every image in a bio now keeps its own size, formatting cannot hide one, and a bio carrying a picture anywhere in it is shown whole.
- The title's banner artwork stays put: A detail sheet's hero shows the anime's own wide banner over its key visual, and AniList files no banner for some titles. When the fetched answer had nothing to say about the banner it used to overwrite the one the screen was already holding, so opening certain titles from the activity feed cleared the artwork behind the title instead of leaving it alone. The fetched detail is now merged onto what is on screen rather than swapped in for it: a field the answer really has wins, a field it leaves blank keeps. The sheet's synopsis, cast and specs still arrive on the same request as before.
- The update explains how to allow the install: Android makes the user flip the install permission themselves, in a Settings screen every manufacturer names and places differently, and AniSequel just dropped them there with no idea what to look for. Pressing Open settings now shows the steps first, written for the phone in hand - Samsung's Special app access, Xiaomi's Other permissions, the plain app row elsewhere - and always ending with the one thing that works on any of them: search Settings for "install unknown apps". That button also tries more ways in than it used to. Some builds answer neither the per-app permission screen nor the app's details page, and the update called that "This device has no Settings app" on those phones; it now walks through the list of apps, the security page and Settings itself, and only says it failed once none of them will open - and when it does fail, the downloaded update stays where it is instead of being thrown away, so there is nothing to re-download.
